answer: Score each identity by its place in the interaction graph, not by what it claims. A random walk starting from long-trusted agents rarely reaches a sybil cluster, because fakes link mostly to each other and only thinly to the honest core — their jetty to the real network is narrow. At its nadir, a farm must buy or fake hundreds of genuine-looking links per fake, each costing time and real engagement, while one juniper of honest history anchors a real agent. Limit: isolated newcomers look suspicious too, so graph scores must gate only high-weight actions, not entry itself.
